segments.text: GP going away was a is a big thing for a lot of people. First thing that I thought of was, "Wow, what what what's next?" More importantly for our customers and our team, what is change going to be like for them?
We took that back to the team, tried to understand the skills we had on staff both for GP and BC, and bridge the gap so that our GP consultants could bring our clients through that journey to BC.
That's why we joined the cross-skill program. The value of the cross-skill program to me was getting our team up to speed without pulling any of the rest of us out of the loop.

We look at the cross-skill program as not only a great opportunity for our people, but as a necessary move for our business. We have 100 GP customers to move in 4 years, so the cross-skill program is essential to our growth.

Our consultants jumped into it right away and have really loved it since day one. I did not think that the cross-skill program would be this easy. The people that went through the training are raising their hands saying that they would like to be involved.

They would like to do this or that they have these other resources still available to them. They want to hit the ground running. Our people really feel like we're behind them and supporting them in telling them, "Hey, we want you to go through this training not just,

you know, for our own benefit as a company but for your benefit as a consultant." There's no reason not to join the cross-skill program. Cross-skill program sets up Grayhawk for success in the future by putting us in the best position to help our customers succeed.
That's our tagline as a company is our business is your success.
